audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer gave Akali all seven stages while the full layer gave Lissandra all seven, and the packet flags the contradiction directly: 'Akali wins only 47.29% but the chart gives Akali 7/7 stages vs 0'.
audit.why: This is Akali's worst matchup in the slice and the full layer already grades it HARD 8/10. The content chart is the wrong one — and its 'why' lines were built on an invented mechanic, so the whole content-layer narrative had to move with it.
audit.corrected: win[0..6] flipped to Lissandra, matching the full layer's phases[N].side, which already reads Lissandra on all seven rows. whys[0..6], early, mid, late, all four spikes and the wants lines rewritten from her side.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was written as an Akali spike: 'your Perfect Execution can finish her before she recovers'.
audit.why: Level 6 is the wall, not the spike. Frozen Tomb cast on herself makes her untargetable AND invulnerable while healing — an execute ultimate spent into it is refunded to her. It is 120s at rank 1, which is the real spike timer to track.
audit.corrected: Level 6 rewritten as her window; your windows are the 24s Glacial Path gap and the 120s after Frozen Tomb.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer repeatedly cited a 'self-root Ice Shard' that 'doesn't burst you outright' (whys[4], spikes[1], mid).
audit.why: There is no self-root on Ice Shard. Ice Shard (Q) is a 725-range spear that slows, and its shards pass THROUGH the first target to hit enemies behind — so a minion does not shield you from it. The self-cast is Frozen Tomb (R). The decisive interaction the page missed: Ring of Frost is centred on Lissandra and roots nearby enemies without targeting anyone, so Twilight Shroud's 'unable to be selected by enemy spells and attacks' does not prevent it — the shroud is not an answer to her root.
audit.corrected: Fabricated mechanic removed everywhere; Ring of Frost (450 range, 10s at rank 1, 40 mana) written in as the reason the shroud fails here; Ice Shard's pass-through written into wave management.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns named Glacial Path as matchup-defining but carried no number.
audit.why: Glacial Path is 24s at rank 1 (12s only when maxed) and she is immobile for every second of it — the single largest punishable cooldown in the lane, and the only reason the matchup is playable at all.
audit.corrected: 24s written in and used as the commit trigger in dosFull[0], spikes[0], wants.you[0] and report[9].

audit.whatIsWrong: No Grievous Wounds note despite Frozen Tomb healing her.
audit.why: Flagged in missingInteractions (needs-antiheal), and it compounds the untargetable window — she leaves the invulnerability healthier than she entered it.
audit.corrected: Itemization line now names Ignite's Grievous Wounds against the Frozen Tomb heal.

audit.whatIsWrong: Wave management assumed hiding behind minions works.
audit.why: 'Shards pass through the target, dealing the same damage to other enemies hit' — Ice Shard is not stopped by the minion you stand behind, which changes where you can legally farm.

notes: This matchup had the largest defect in the slice and the packet had already caught it: the content layer claimed Akali wins 7/7 stages at a 47.29% win rate, while the full layer correctly grades it HARD 8/10 with Lissandra on all seven rows. I flipped the content chart to match the full layer rather than the reverse. The content narrative was built on a mechanic that does not exist — a 'self-root Ice Shard' that 'doesn't burst you' — appearing in whys[4], spikes[1] and mid; the actual self-cast is Frozen Tomb, and it is untargetable and invulnerable, which inverts the level 6 conclusion completely. The full layer's tldr was already accurate and specific ('Her W roots you in the shroud you trusted and her self-R laughs at your all-in') and was left untouched, along with report[0].t. Two mechanics added that were absent everywhere: Ring of Frost is centred on Lissandra and needs no target, so Twilight Shroud's untargetability does not prevent the root; and Ice Shard's shards pass through the first target, so standing behind a minion does not stop the poke.
